title: Deep learning reveals a new seismicity distribution along the Kabaw Fault in central Myanmar
summary: A deep-learning-based catalog pipeline processed 18 months of seismic-array data and located 1,891 shallow earthquakes, more than twice the 849 events in the prior manual catalog. The denser catalog shows that shallow Kabaw Fault seismicity disappears south of about 22.8°N while deeper events occur west of the fault, and it fills part of a previously under-sampled seismicity gap; the authors interpret this contrast as potentially reflecting along-strike variation in deformation associated with oblique Indian-plate subduction.
ai_technology: DEPALORE pipeline using Earthquake Transformer, transfer-learned PickNet, REAL association, NonLinLoc location and HypoDD relocation
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Zhejiang Ocean University; collaborators

evidence.tested: A deep-learning-based catalog pipeline processed 18 months of seismic-array data and located 1,891 shallow earthquakes, more than twice the 849 events in the prior manual catalog.
evidence.unknown: The source reports catalog-derived patterns and offers a tentative tectonic explanation; the catalog contains 1,891 localized events and location uncertainties of several kilometers. The AI enabled detections and resolution, while geological interpretation remains the authors’ analysis.
evidence.ai_role: Deep-learning detectors and phase-picking models extracted seismic arrivals from continuous array waveforms; association and location stages produced the higher-completeness catalog from which researchers interpreted fault patterns.
